title: 06. Typing & Models: Validators
summary: Pydantic validators are custom functions that run during validation to add your own business rules:

sections.title: Concept Explanation (Junior Developer Style)
sections.body:
Pydantic validators are **custom functions** that run during validation to add your own business rules:

```
@field_validator    → validates/transforms a SINGLE field
@model_validator    → validates/transforms the ENTIRE model (cross-field)
```

> 🧠 Think of validators as **custom security guards** 👮 beyond the basic bouncers. `Field(gt=0)` is the basic check. `@field_validator` is your custom detective who does deeper checks.

### Validator Modes:

```
mode="before"  → runs BEFORE Pydantic's type validation
                 → input is raw (str, dict, etc.)
                 → good for: parsing, transformation

mode="after"   → runs AFTER Pydantic's type validation
                 → input is already the correct type
                 → good for: business rules on clean data

mode="wrap"    → you call the next validator yourself
                 → most flexible, least common
```

quiz.question: What is the difference between @field_validator and @model_validator?
options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > FastAPI is built ON TOP of Pydantic — every parameter, body, response, and query string is a Pydantic model.
5-Year Exp Answer: > InitVar in inherited dataclasses requires careful handling because __post_init__ signature changes: > > > > The child's __post_init__ must accept…
5-Year Exp Answer: > Generic models use Python's Generic[T] to create reusable model templates parameterized by type.
5-Year Exp Answer: > @field_validator("field_name") validates/transforms a single field in isolation — it only sees that field's value. @model_validator validates the…
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: @field_validator("field_name") validates/transforms a single field in isolation — it only sees that field's value. @model_validator validates the entire model — it has access to ALL fields and can check cross-field relationships. Execution order: (1) @model_validator(mode="before") — first, with raw input dict. (2) Field validators — field by field.

quiz.question: What does mode="before" vs mode="after" mean in validators?
options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > An Enum (enumeration) is a set of named, immutable constants grouped under a type.
5-Year Exp Answer: > Never expose raw Pydantic ValidationError to clients — transform it: > > > > Log the full error internally, return clean user-facing messages.
5-Year Exp Answer: > metadata is a read-only mapping (dict-like) attached to a field for use by external code — the dataclass itself ignores it completely.
5-Year Exp Answer: > mode="before": validator runs BEFORE Pydantic's type parsing.
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: mode="before": validator runs BEFORE Pydantic's type parsing. The input v is RAW — could be string, dict, list, None.

quiz.question: How do you validate one field based on the value of another field?
options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > __post_init__() is a special method automatically called by the dataclass-generated __init__() AFTER all field assignments are complete.
5-Year Exp Answer: > In lax mode (default), Pydantic tries to coerce values: "42" → 42, "true" → True, "2024-01-15" → date.
5-Year Exp Answer: > Yes to both! Enums are full classes — members can have methods, properties, and classmethods: > > > > For multiple values, __init__ receives all values after self.
5-Year Exp Answer: > Use @model_validator(mode="after") — it has access to all fields as self.field_name: > > > > For mode="before" (raw dict), access other fields via…
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: Use @model_validator(mode="after") — it has access to all fields as self.field_name: For mode="before" (raw dict), access other fields via data["field_name"]. In @field_validator (v2), use info.data to access previously-validated fields: Important: info.data only contains fields validated BEFORE this one — field order matters!

quiz.question: How do you return a transformed value from a validator?
options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > Pydantic v2 (2023+) is a complete rewrite in Rust — 5-50x faster than v1.
5-Year Exp Answer: > These are number comparison constraints: gt = greater than (strict, excludes the value itself), ge = greater than or equal (inclusive), lt = less…
5-Year Exp Answer: > Yes to both! Enums are full classes — members can have methods, properties, and classmethods: > > > > For multiple values, __init__ receives all values after self.
5-Year Exp Answer: > Simply return the transformed value from the validator — Pydantic uses the returned value as the field's value: > > > > If you don't return (return…
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: Simply return the transformed value from the validator — Pydantic uses the returned value as the field's value: If you don't return (return None implicitly), the field becomes None! This is a common bug. Always explicitly return the value (transformed or original) from validators.

quiz.question: How do you raise multiple validation errors from a single validator?
options: 5-Year Exp Answer: > eq=False disables __eq__ generation — equality comparison falls back to identity (is) comparison from object.
5-Year Exp Answer: > compare=False excludes a field from BOTH __eq__ and ordering comparisons (__lt__, etc.).
5-Year Exp Answer: > The child dataclass generates its own __eq__ that compares ALL fields — both parent fields and child fields.
5-Year Exp Answer: > Single raise ValueError("message") gives one error.
quiz.explanation: 5-Year Exp Answer: Single raise ValueError("message") gives one error. For multiple errors, collect them and raise once: In Pydantic v2, you can also use PydanticCustomError for more control over error types and codes. For model validators returning multiple field errors, raise ValueError as a list — Pydantic converts it to multiple errors: --- --- S1.
